components.basis: Composite of D-P3-002-GOAL-01..04, each judged covered on the route at its required standing (definitions plus written proofs). The original row (classical analytic tableaux for propositional and first-order logic with countermodel extraction and completeness; spec/inventory/2026-09-06/complete-requirement-ledger.json lines 25604-25615) is met for both the propositional and the first-order (equality-free and equality) calculi; its notes (absent book-wide apart from the many-valued matrix tableau; also listed in B3 automation and the cross-cutting list) are diagnostic and impose no further bounded subcomponent. The hypotheses actually used (finite roots, sentences in the first-order case, T for equality-free roots and T-equality otherwise) are announced in the text (w02-p02-014 lines 21-36, 359-379), so no narrower domain is unannounced.

Rules: the seven expansion rules and the closure rule are displayed on sheet:tableaux-cpl (lines 12-19, rendered on route at classical-and-constructive-calculi.tex 204) and fixed in the body by the premise/alternatives table with linear and branching kinds (w02-p02-014 lines 66-94). Branches: a branch is a list with a set of marked positions, occurrences are positions, expansion steps append alternatives and mark the principal occurrence without deleting it (lines 95-109); tableaux are last members of expansion sequences (110-114), reconciled with the drawn tree (122-133). Closure: a branch is closed iff it contains bottom or a complementary pair, a tableau is closed iff every branch is (100-102, 114; propositional-hilbert-tableaux 138-142). Input convention: root branch lists each member of Gamma once with no marks; satisfiability, consequence (Gamma plus the literal negation, listed once) and validity tests (lines 41-58; propositional-hilbert-tableaux 144-148; sheet line 11). Saturation and finished tableaux are defined (115-118). Every element of the success condition is present; no failure condition holds (the language is the handbook's full primitive language, nothing is cited in place of a definition).

Quantifier rules: gamma rules for forall and not-exists and delta rules for exists and not-forall on sheet:tableaux-fol (lines 23-26) and as tasks/steps in def:p02-w02-p02-014-fol-branch (w02-p02-014 lines 428-457). Equality rules: tableau reflexivity and left-to-right replacement on atomic sentences with the single-occurrence formula condition (def:p02-w02-p02-014-fol-equality, lines 392-416; sheet lines 27-28), with the calculus split T / T-equality fixed in def:p02-w02-p02-014-fol-setting (359-390). Freshness: a delta step uses the parameter of least index not occurring on the branch (446-451, 489-490; sheet 25-26), and the failure of a non-fresh step is exhibited (790-798). Instantiation: gamma and reflexivity tasks range over every closed term of the parameter-extended language, not only terms on the branch (432-435, 452-455, 490-491; first-order-calculi-supplement 124-129). Fairness: def:p02-fol-tableau defines fair branches by the fixed enumeration (first-order-calculi-supplement 127-129); saturation of finite and limit branches is defined (470-479) and identified with fair and saturated (483-488), including the T-equality reflexivity/replacement tasks (434-439, 496-497; sheet line 15); an unfair branch is shown not to be a countermodel (777-788). All elements are present; nothing is cited in place of a definition.

Propositional: soundness of closure (thm:p02-w02-p02-014-soundness, lines 174-184) proved in annex lines 97-121 from the case-split lemma (155-161; annex 10-69); countermodel extraction from an open saturated branch by the truth lemma (204-207; annex 164-196) using the branch invariants (163-172; annex 71-95); completeness and read-off (212-221; annex 198-214) with termination (186-199; annex 123-162) and the consequence/validity corollary with countervaluation (223-234; annex 216-241); thm:p02-tableau-adequacy (propositional-hilbert-tableaux 151-163) is proved from these in annex/p02/propositional-hilbert.tex 69-86. First-order (T and T-equality): sound case splits (499-521; annex 325-377), invariants (523-537; annex 379-420), soundness (539-552; annex 422-454); extraction from an open saturated (fair), finite or limit, branch via Hintikka sets, the congruence lemma and the quotient Herbrand truth lemma (557-623; annex 456-628); completeness, consequence and countermodel clauses (683-700; annex 737-760) through the fair procedure (660-681; annex 630-735); thm:p02-fol-tableau-adequacy (first-order-calculi-supplement 137-160) is proved in annex/p02/first-order-calculi-supplement.tex 63-83. Every proof writes its steps; the external dependencies used (unique readability, substitution lemma, substitution complexity and free variables, reduct invariance) are themselves proved on the route. No citation stands in for a proof and no unproved dependency is presented as proved.

Terminating propositional decision: the systematic procedure (def:p02-w02-p02-014-procedure, lines 236-253) halts within 2^(mu+1)-2 steps and decides satisfiability, validity and finite consequence with countervaluations (thm:p02-w02-p02-014-decision, 255-265; annex 243-273, including effectiveness). First-order semidecision: the failure of the termination argument is proved (finite open branches carrying a universal or negated existential occurrence are never saturated, 319-337; annex 275-299); the fair staged procedure (633-658) halts with unsatisfiable exactly on unsatisfiable finite inputs (thm:p02-w02-p02-014-fol-semidecision, 660-681; annex 630-735). Infinite branch construction: clause 2 of that theorem builds an open, saturated, fair and infinite limit branch when the procedure does not halt, proved by the good-branch construction in annex 649-702; the example forall x Px exhibits a satisfiable root with no finite finished tableau and an infinite saturated branch (758-775). The proof boundary (800-816) contrasts decision with semidecision and marks the only cited input (thm:fol-validity-undecidable, whose status is cited at restoration/inherited-08248-08305.tex 9-14) as used for a concluding remark only, so no cited result is presented as proved.
